title: STALEMATE! STALEMATE! STALEMATE!
summary: Keep adjusting the king and knight, then underpromote to avoid the final stalemate.

nodes.question: Why is promotion not automatically safe?
nodes.explanation: The rook can check on the c-file and exploit either a fork or a stalemate. White must coordinate the king and knight before choosing the promotion piece.

nodes.question: Can White promote after covering c3?
nodes.explanation: Ne2 covers c3, but ...Ka5 has arranged a stalemate if the knight captures a sacrificed rook.

nodes.question: Does moving the king remove every stalemate?
nodes.explanation: White has attacked the rook with Kc4. Its retreat to d6 sets another c-file sacrifice against a queen.

nodes.question: Which piece should the pawn become?
nodes.explanation: Black’s king on b6 has no safe square if White adds a queen. A rook leaves a flight square and keeps the game winning.

branches.title: Coordinate first and promote to a rook
commentary: Begin from the complete five-piece saved opening board.
Ne2 protects c3, meeting the rook’s potential checking fork after promotion.
Ka5 arranges a different defense: a capture on c3 can leave Black stalemated.
Kc4 attacks Rd3 and changes the king coverage before White promotes.
Rd6 retreats while preparing another rook sacrifice on the c-file.
Nd4 covers c6. White improves the knight before allowing the rook’s next checking move.
Rc6+ offers the rook with check, still trying to exploit the king’s restricted squares.
Nxc6+ removes the rook with check against Ka5. White now has a knight and pawn against the king.
Kb6 answers the knight check, attacks both c7 and Nc6, and sets the final stalemate trap.
c8=R underpromotes. The rook keeps Black a legal flight square while preserving the exact win. The selected branch ends at this checked rook-and-knight ending, not an immediate mate.
branches.explanation: c8=R underpromotes. The rook keeps Black a legal flight square while preserving the exact win. The selected branch ends at this checked rook-and-knight ending, not an immediate mate.

branches.title: Promote before moving the king
commentary: Compare a queen promotion after Ne2 and ...Ka5.
c8=Q gives away the win. The extra queen helps close Black’s flight squares.
Rc3+ sacrifices the rook with check, inviting the knight to remove Black’s only movable piece.
Nxc3 is actual stalemate. Ka5 is not checked; Qc8 covers a6, Nc3 covers a4, and Kc5 covers b4, b5 and b6.
branches.explanation: Nxc3 is actual stalemate. Ka5 is not checked; Qc8 covers a6, Nc3 covers a4, and Kc5 covers b4, b5 and b6.

branches.title: Promote before improving the knight
commentary: Compare immediate queen promotion after Kc4 and ...Rd6.
c8=Q gives away the win again. The queen can capture a checking rook, but that capture can freeze the enemy king.
Rc6+ checks Kc4 and attacks Qc8 along the c-file.
Qxc6 is actual stalemate. Qc6 covers a6, a4 and b6, while Kc4 covers b4 and b5. Ka5 has no move and is not checked.
branches.explanation: Qxc6 is actual stalemate. Qc6 covers a6, a4 and b6, while Kc4 covers b4 and b5. Ka5 has no move and is not checked.

branches.title: Choose a queen in the final position
commentary: Compare maximum material with the rook underpromotion after ...Kb6.
c8=Q is actual stalemate. Qc8 covers a6, b7, c7 and c6; Nc6 covers a5 and a7; Kc4 covers b5 and c5. Kb6 is not checked and has no legal move.
branches.explanation: c8=Q is actual stalemate. Qc8 covers a6, b7, c7 and c6; Nc6 covers a5 and a7; Kc4 covers b5 and c5. Kb6 is not checked and has no legal move.

exercises.prompt: Why can protecting c3 with a knight still fail?
exercises.answer: After c8=Q Rc3+ Nxc3, the queen, knight and king cover every square around Ka5 without checking it. Removing the rook leaves Black no legal move.

exercises.prompt: What does rook promotion deliberately give up?
exercises.answer: A rook omits the queen’s diagonal control of a6, leaving the black king a legal move. White avoids stalemate and keeps a winning rook-and-knight ending.

startContext: Begin from the full five-piece source board. Three independently checked actual stalemates are contrasted with the source’s king/knight preparation and rook underpromotion. The selected branches do not claim an exhaustive tree of every rook defense.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
